title: Zookeeper Salary: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to calculate your zookeeper salary from an hourly rate using a 38-hour week, 52-week year. Includes award rates, casual loading, super, and tax.
salarySummary: A zookeeper earning $26.44 per hour (the 2026 National Minimum Wage) working 38 hours a week for 52 weeks would have an annual salary of $52,265 before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the formula to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super.

faqs.q: Does a zookeeper salary include casual loading?
faqs.a: If you are employed as a casual zookeeper, your hourly rate should include a 25% casual loading on top of the base award rate. For example, if the base rate is $26.44, the casual rate would be $33.05 per hour. Always check your award or enterprise agreement.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated for a zookeeper?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026). It does not come out of your hourly rate. For a full-time zookeeper earning $52,265 gross, the employer would contribute an additional $6,272 in super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Zookeeper Salary

If you're a zookeeper or considering a career in animal care, knowing how to turn an hourly rate into an annual figure is essential. Whether you're negotiating a job offer or checking your pay, the conversion is straightforward: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. This article explains the formula, the key pay rules from the Fair Work Ombudsman and Fair Work Commission, and how tax and super affect your take-home pay.

### The Standard 38-Hour Week

Most full-time positions in Australia are based on a 38-hour week. When we talk about a zookeeper salary, we assume 38 ordinary hours unless your award or agreement says otherwise. The calculation is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, at the 2026 National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, the annual salary is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,264.64 (rounded to $52,265). This is the minimum for award/agreement-free employees, but most zookeepers are covered by an award.

### Award Rates for Zookeepers

Zookeepers are typically covered by the *Animal Care and Veterinary Services Award* or a similar modern award. From 1 July 2026, award minimum wages increased by 4.75% following the Annual Wage Review. The Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database provides the exact classification rates, allowances, and penalty rates. Always check the relevant pay guide on the Fair Work Ombudsman website for your specific classification.

### Casual Loading and Part-Time Work

If you work as a casual zookeeper, your hourly rate includes a 25% casual loading. This is paid on top of the base award rate. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. When using our [timesheet](/), you can enter your base hourly rate and check the casual loading box to add the 25% on top. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading into that field.

For part-time zookeepers, the same hourly rate applies, but you work fewer hours per week. Your annual salary is simply your hourly rate × your agreed weekly hours × 52.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a full-time zookeeper on the minimum award rate (say $26.44/hr), weekly pay is $1,004.90, so fortnightly pay is $2,009.80 before tax and super.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Superannuation is an extra 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. It does not reduce your take-home pay. For a full-time zookeeper earning $52,265, the employer contributes $6,272 in super (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830). This is a key part of your total remuneration package.

### Tax on Your Zookeeper Salary

Your annual gross pay is taxed according to the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on the excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45% on the excess over $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of generally 2% of your taxable income. For a $52,265 salary, the tax would be approximately $7,092 plus Medicare of $1,045, leaving about $44,128 take-home pay. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a detailed estimate.

### Using the Hourly to Annual Conversion

Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool helps you quickly see the annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Remember: the calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates or allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It's an estimate, not a binding determination.

### Summary

Whether you're a zookeeper or any other worker, converting your hourly rate to an annual salary is simple: hourly × 38 × 52. Check your award for the correct classification rate, add casual loading if applicable, and remember that super is paid on top. For the most accurate figures, refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides and the Fair Work Commission's database. Use our [reference tables](/data) for quick lookups of minimum wages and tax brackets.
